title: What is OTP and Why You Must Never Share It?
subtitle: One-Time Password — The Digital Lock to Your Bank Account
summary: An OTP (One-Time Password) is a confidential 6-digit verification code generated by your bank to authenticate a single transaction. It is the digital key guarding your hard-earned money. Legitimate bank staff, police, lottery officials, and utility agents will NEVER ask for your OTP.
rule: Golden Rule: If anyone asks for an OTP over call or SMS, hang up immediately. Disclosing your OTP grants instant access to drain your bank account.
do: Always read the transaction amount and merchant name mentioned in the OTP SMS before acting.
dont: Never share your OTP under promises of lotteries, KYC updates, cashbacks, or electricity bill offers.

video_steps.title: Bank Dispatches Secret Code
video_steps.desc: Whenever a transaction starts, your bank sends a confidential 6-digit code to your registered mobile.

video_steps.title: Fraudster Impersonates Authority
video_steps.desc: The scammer calls claiming: 'I am your bank manager; share the SMS verification code to keep your card active'.

video_steps.title: Account Drained Instantly
video_steps.desc: As soon as you speak the 6 digits, the fraudster completes the unauthorized transfer to siphon your money.

video_steps.title: Golden Defense Rule
video_steps.desc: Real banks never ask for OTPs over the phone. Hang up instantly and report fraudulent calls to 1930.

topic: How to Keep ATM PIN Safe?
title: How to Keep Your ATM PIN Confidential and Secure?
subtitle: 4-Digit Secret Code — The Physical Master Key
summary: Your ATM PIN is a 4-digit personal identification number that authorizes cash withdrawals. Never write your PIN on the back of your ATM card or store it on paper in your wallet. Never disclose it to store clerks, friends, or security guards.
rule: Rule: Always shield the ATM keypad with your other hand when withdrawing cash. Never accept withdrawal assistance from strangers.
do: Cover the keypad with your hand while typing your PIN and change your PIN every 3 to 6 months.
dont: Never write your PIN on the debit card, and never hand your card to security guards or bystanders.

video_steps.title: Memorize Your 4-Digit PIN
video_steps.desc: Your ATM PIN should only live in your memory. Never write it on your debit card or a slip of paper.

video_steps.title: Beware of Shoulder Surfers
video_steps.desc: Scammers often linger nearby or position miniature cameras above keypads to record your PIN entry.

video_steps.title: Shield Keypad With Free Hand
video_steps.desc: Form a physical roof over the numeric keypad with your free hand so no camera or bystander can see your code.

video_steps.title: Decline Stranger Assistance
video_steps.desc: If the ATM card gets stuck, inform bank officials inside the branch. Never let strangers handle your card.

title: When Should You Enter Your UPI PIN and When NEVER?
subtitle: PIN is ONLY for Sending Money — Never for Receiving
summary: Your UPI PIN is the final authorization that debits funds from your bank account. You enter your UPI PIN ONLY when you are transferring money to someone or paying a merchant bill. You NEVER need to enter your UPI PIN to receive money, accept refunds, or claim cashbacks.
rule: Golden Rule: Enter PIN = Money OUT! Receiving funds requires ZERO PIN.
do: Only enter your PIN when you are knowingly initiating a payment or paying an authentic bill.
dont: Never enter your UPI PIN to claim lottery prizes, subsidies, buyer deposits, or lucky draw cashbacks.

video_steps.title: PIN Purpose: Debit Authorization
video_steps.desc: Entering your UPI PIN commands your bank to deduct money from your account and send it away.

video_steps.title: Scammer's Bait: 'Collect Money'
video_steps.desc: A buyer on OLX claims: 'I have credited ₹5,000 for your item, enter your UPI PIN to accept it'.

video_steps.title: Money Siphoned Instead
video_steps.desc: The moment you enter your PIN, ₹5,000 is immediately debited from your account to the fraudster.

video_steps.title: Unbreakable Safety Rule
video_steps.desc: Receiving money NEVER requires entering your PIN. If anyone tells you to enter PIN to get funds, refuse!

title: What is QR Code Fraud and How to Stay Protected?
subtitle: Scanning a QR Code Always Sends Money — Never Receives
summary: A QR code is simply a visual shortcut to a merchant's payment address. Fraudsters send QR codes over WhatsApp or online marketplaces saying 'Scan this code to receive ₹5,000 cashback or government grant'. Be warned: Scanning a QR code always initiates an outgoing payment from your account.
rule: Rule: Never scan a QR code sent by an unknown person to receive funds.
do: When scanning a shopkeeper's QR code, always verify the merchant's verified business name on screen.
dont: Never scan QR codes sent via WhatsApp, email, or OLX claiming to deposit money into your account.

video_steps.title: How QR Codes Actually Work
video_steps.desc: A QR code represents a payment destination address used solely to transfer money out to a vendor.

video_steps.title: The Cashback / Lottery Trap
video_steps.desc: The fraudster texts an attractive QR graphic: 'Scan here to claim your government subsidy of ₹3,000'.

video_steps.title: Payment Screen Triggers
video_steps.desc: Scanning instantly opens your UPI app's checkout debit screen, ready to authorize a payout.

video_steps.title: Shield Your Wallet
video_steps.desc: You never need to scan a QR code to receive money. Delete unsolicited QR images immediately!

topic: How to Identify Fake Bank Calls?
title: How to Identify Fake Bank Calls and Stay Protected?
subtitle: Urgent Threats to Suspend Accounts — The Primary Scam Weapon
summary: Fraudsters impersonate bank managers or CSPDCL electricity officials over the phone. They fabricate urgency: 'Your bank account, debit card, or electricity will be terminated in 2 hours unless you verify details or download AnyDesk'. Genuine banks and government departments never issue phone threats.
rule: Truth: Legitimate banks never threaten immediate account suspension over phone calls or ask for remote access.
do: Whenever a caller threatens suspension, hang up and visit your local bank branch directly.
dont: Never install remote screen-sharing apps (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, RustDesk) or send debit card photos.

video_steps.title: Urgent Panic Creation
video_steps.desc: The caller barks: 'I am calling from the bank head office; your account will be suspended today'.

video_steps.title: Remote Access App Trap
video_steps.desc: He instructs: 'To resolve this immediately, download AnyDesk or QuickSupport from Play Store'.

video_steps.title: Total Phone Takeover
video_steps.desc: Once installed, the scammer watches your phone screen remotely, capturing bank passwords and OTPs.

video_steps.title: Hang Up and Report!
video_steps.desc: Do not panic! Real banks never demand screen-sharing apps. Disconnect immediately and call 1930.
